title: Are CPG Companies Ready for Agentic Commerce?
gist: BCG argues AI shopping agents are restructuring the CPG funnel end to end: 96% of AI shoppers use AI for discovery, AI traffic could pass organic search in the US by 2028, and 20-30% of one CPG player's online revenue is at risk. It prescribes three reinforcing plays (GEO at 1-5% revenue gain, owned agents with ~25% higher conversion, and ecosystem integration) and warns GEO alone leads to commoditization.

themes.theme: Shopper behavior is moving to AI agents

insights.claim: Among US consumers, 80% already use AI and nearly half of those use it to shop; among AI shoppers 96% use it for discovery, 80% for consideration and 24% for purchasing, while only 4% would let an agent complete a purchase alone.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Agents are a top-of-funnel gatekeeper first and a checkout rail later; near-term economics sit in discovery and consideration, not autonomous purchase.
insights.quote: Among these AI shoppers, 96% use it for product discovery and 80% for consideration

insights.claim: Traditional search traffic is shrinking as LLM traffic explodes: organic traffic fell 10% in 2024 versus 87% growth in LLM traffic; AI referrals were under 1% of visits to leading European retail and brand sites in late 2025, could reach 5% by end-2026, and AI traffic is expected to overtake organic search in the US as early as 2028.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
entities: BCG CCI Global Consumer Radar Survey 2025
insights.so_what: A datable trajectory for the erosion of SEO-dependent traffic models; watch publishers, search-ad and affiliate exposure.
insights.quote: AI-driven traffic is expected to overtake organic search in the US as early as 2028
insights.locator: The Funnel Is Transforming from End to End

insights.claim: Agent-mediated shopping makes decisions more methodical and multibrand: about 70% of AI shoppers compare product attributes and around 50% run pre-purchase price comparisons, reducing impulse-driven purchases.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Price and attribute transparency erodes brand-equity premia and impulse categories.
insights.locator: The Funnel Is Transforming from End to End

insights.claim: Exposure varies by category: 52% of skincare shoppers go straight to loved brands and 42% rely on research, whereas only 35% of household-appliance buyers go direct to a preferred brand and 59% are research-led.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Research-led, low-loyalty categories will be disrupted first; loyalty-heavy categories like skincare have more runway.
insights.locator: The Funnel Is Transforming from End to End

insights.claim: As the funnel compresses, discovery and purchase will likely eventually happen in a single interaction, which may make post-purchase experience harder for direct-to-consumer CPG brands.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: DTC brands need service and automated replenishment in place, or lose the relationship after the agent closes the sale.
insights.locator: The Funnel Is Transforming from End to End

themes.theme: Revenue at risk and readiness gap

insights.claim: An assessment for a global CPG player suggested 20% to 30% of its online revenue could be at risk as discovery shifts to AI search.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Sizing anchor for downside from non-visibility; online revenue of CPG names is exposed to AI discovery shifts.
insights.quote: an assessment conducted for a global CPG player’s suggests that 20% to 30% of its online revenue could be at risk

insights.claim: Most CPG companies are unprepared: only 41% have begun building some agentic AI capabilities and 59% report no meaningful capabilities today.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A large readiness gap implies early movers can take share and laggards face dispersion.
insights.quote: the remaining 59% report no meaningful capabilities in this area today

insights.claim: Planned CPG investment skews to defensive plays: 65% plan GEO and 47% product data structuring, versus 41% owned agents and 35% ecosystem integration.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Industry spend is crowding into the commodity layer, leaving the offensive layers less contested for now.

themes.theme: Three plays: GEO, owned agents, ecosystem

insights.claim: Generative engine optimization (AI-readable data, structured claims, schema-marked FAQs and R&D-based scientific content) is a must-have defensive move; pilots yield 1% to 5% incremental revenue.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Low-cost, near-term revenue lever, but evidence is early pilot-level and self-reported by the consultancy.
insights.quote: CPG companies piloting GEO are already experiencing a 1% to 5% incremental increase in revenues

insights.claim: A global luxury fashion group prioritized 500 consumer prompts and ran about 10 pilots starting with structured data and metadata; its AI-search citation rate more than doubled in eight weeks and LLM-sourced traffic more than quadrupled in six months.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Technical fixes can move AI visibility quickly, implying fast payback but also fast imitation.
insights.quote: its brand site’s citation rate in AI search more than doubled, and within six months LLM-sourced traffic more than quadrupled

insights.claim: Owned brand agents capture first-party data and lift conversion: a leading personal-care company sees chat users convert about 25% more often, and campaigns powered by agent data generate twice the ROI of those using traditional first-party data.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Owned agents may turn conversation data into a durable moat; claimed ROI uplift on digital media up to 50%.
insights.quote: shoppers who chat with its AI advisor convert to buyers about 25% more often than those who do not

insights.claim: Pilots of owned agents and ecosystem integration are reported to drive 3% to 10% revenue growth, above the 1% to 5% from GEO alone.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Suggests higher upside for offensive plays, though figures are consultancy-reported and not independently verified.

insights.claim: GEO alone will not differentiate in the medium term as adoption becomes widespread; brands that only invest in GEO and data sharing defensively risk being commoditized.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Treat GEO as table stakes; a GEO-only strategy is not a moat and should not be credited as a competitive advantage.
insights.quote: a brand that only invests in GEO and data sharing as a defensive play can become commoditized

insights.claim: The winning model is a flywheel: better data and content strengthen owned agents, better agents win ecosystem integration, integration expands reach and monetization, and partnerships return richer data.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Data compounding favors early movers; the gap between leaders and laggards should widen over time.

insights.claim: Retailer data access is restricted: 32% of retailers give direct data access only to selected agents and 87% do not share customer data with agents at all, so brands need proprietary data and an owned agent as bargaining chips.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Retailers are gatekeepers of customer data, so brand leverage depends on bringing differentiated data.
insights.quote: 87% do not share customer data with agents at all

insights.claim: Brands that delay will negotiate ecosystem partnerships later from weakness, with fewer partnership slots, reduced leverage and a widening data gap.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: First-mover advantage in agent partnerships; a slot-scarcity argument that is plausible but unproven.
insights.locator: The Window for Action is Narrowing

insights.claim: Retailers are building agents unevenly: Amazon and Walmart have proprietary AI agents, Carrefour and Target launched dedicated apps within ChatGPT, and many others rely on passive discovery via third-party AI engines; Google's Universal Commerce Protocol enables discovery-to-checkout journeys.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Control of the agent layer is becoming a retail competitive axis; retailer-owned agents may squeeze brand influence.

insights.claim: A structural tension exists: LLM platforms have users but often incomplete or inaccurate product data, brand sites have content but little organic traffic, and retailers build agents often without sufficient brand input.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Whoever resolves the data-quality gap between platforms and brands can capture value; opening for brand data feeds and intermediaries.

insights.claim: Agents make traditional discounts invisible and compress margins through instant price comparison, so CPGs should build real-time structured promotion feeds and invest in data quality and claim authority, which BCG argues drive more volume than discounts in an agentic setting.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Promotional intensity and trade-spend models face pressure; margin risk for price-led CPG.

insights.claim: AI agents ignore traditional ads, so media is shifting toward agent-influencing formats such as sponsored prompts and in-agent ads, which carry transparency and trust issues.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Pressure on legacy ad inventory and a new ad market emerging inside LLM platforms.
insights.quote: AI agents ignore traditional ads; as a result, agentic media formats are emerging

insights.claim: Agents reduce perceived retailer differentiation and open direct-to-consumer pathways, letting brands with purchase-enabled agents capture relationships and margin currently intermediated by retailers.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Potential shift of margin from retailers to brands, but contingent on brands driving consumers to their own agents, which BCG itself calls costly.

insights.claim: Brands should build multi-item, routine-based baskets via agent-readable product interdependencies (as in beauty) so agents move beyond single-product recommendations.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Cross-sell via data-structured bundles could raise basket size in agent-led shopping.

insights.claim: Value will shift from aggregate to precision reach, offering the right content, agent or partner for each shopper mission.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Marketing efficiency may depend on mission-level targeting rather than broad reach.
insights.locator: The Window for Action is Narrowing
